intro:
Approach to Wilno

April 15th, 1919

There is no front here in the sense the staff manuals mean. There is a railway, there are four towns on it, and between them there is nobody at all - the divisions that should be holding this ground are in the Ukraine and on the Don, because that is where the war is being decided. What Lithuania and Byelorussia have is a screen: my detachment, a half-strength brigade of the Western Division, and a great deal of empty country.

Pilsudski is coming for Wilno with cavalry moving off the roads and infantry following on the rails. He is not trying to break us; he is trying to get behind us, and against a screen that works. Moscow's instruction is plain and I will not pretend it is generous: the Wilno group is not to be encircled, and the road south is to stay open until the Soviet institutions and the rolling stock are out of the city.

So this is a delaying action, and it is scored as one. Hold the towns on the withdrawal road until the clock runs out. If their forward assembly area is thinner than it looks, take it and the whole advance loses a week.

Victory conditions:
- Hold Olita (9,18), Orany (16,20) and Lida (23,27) at the last turn - three for a brilliant victory, two for a victory, one for a tactical victory.
- Or take their assembly area at (15,27).

briliant.text:
The road south is open and the towns on it are still ours at the last hour, which is what I was told to deliver.

I will not dress it up beyond that. Wilno itself will not be held - their cavalry is already north of us and the city has one battalion and a printing press in it. But the Western Division comes out as a division, the Soviet workers of the city have had four days to leave, and the trains went south loaded instead of being taken on the sidings.

The Polish papers will call this the liberation of a Polish city. Two thirds of the countryside around it speaks Byelorussian and will find out this summer what liberation means when the estates come back with the army.

They were across the road before the rearguard reached it. The detachment came out in pieces, on foot, by whatever tracks it could find, and left the depot at Lida burning because there was no time to load it.

The Wilno group has effectively ceased to exist as a formation. What is left of it will be reorganised at Molodeczno, and the units that took Wilno now have an open road to the east for as long as it takes us to build another line.

intro:
Assault on Wilno

April 18th, 1919

They came into the city at first light along the railway - an armoured train and a cavalry group that rode through the gap between us and Lida in the dark, dismounted at the station and were in the streets before the garrison knew the line was cut.

The city is going. That was decided at Olita three days ago and nothing I do here changes it. What is not decided is what happens to the twelve thousand men and the four hospital trains north and east of it, and to the Soviet of the city, whose people are being hunted through the Jewish quarter as I write this. The order from the Western Front is to hold the northern and eastern roads open until they are through.

Malaty and Swieciany are the northern gate; the city hexes are the eastern one. Hold them to the last turn. Lida behind them is their forward supply head, and if it can be taken the pursuit stops for a fortnight.

Victory conditions:
- Hold Malaty (24,3), Swieciany (41,6) and Wilno (24,11) at the last turn - three for a brilliant victory, two for a victory, one for a tactical victory.
- Or take Lida (23,27).

briliant.text:
The roads stayed open and the column is through. Rearguard, hospital trains, the Soviet's people and about nine hundred railwaymen who would not have lasted a week in the city.

Wilno is theirs. In the three days after they took it their soldiery went through the Jewish quarter and killed something over sixty people, and their own commission will later put the number lower and call the rest bandits. Remember the number.

We are ordered back to the Berezina line. This is not the end of the business - it is the beginning of a year in which we shall be doing this on ground of their choosing.

The northern road was cut at Swieciany and the eastern one an hour later. What was in the city stayed in the city.

I have no complete return of losses and I will not have one; the men who could get out did so in small parties across country. The Western Front has no reserve to give me and the campaign, as an operation of ours, is over.

intro:
Minsk and the Berezina

August 4th, 1919

The summer has been a lesson in arithmetic. Denikin is at Kharkov and Kolchak has only just been pushed off the Urals, and everything the Republic owns that can march is committed to one or the other. The Western Front has sixteen thousand bayonets on a line four hundred versts long, and orders that begin with the word nevertheless.

Pilsudski is about to take Minsk. Two of his divisions are already past Molodeczno and the Lithuanian-Byelorussian division is coming up the Nieman. He is doing it now, and not in September, because Denikin has told Paris that a Polish state is a temporary administrative inconvenience and will not be recognised by a restored Russia - so Warsaw has a short season in which our defeat is not yet their defeat, and they know it.

The city cannot be held with what I have. The Berezina line behind it can. My task is the railway junctions and the crossings that let the 16th Army get onto that line as an army and not as a crowd, and to keep Minsk itself until the last echelon has cleared it.

Victory conditions:
- Hold Minsk (41,5), Stolpce (30,12) and the crossings at (39,2) and (40,20) at the last turn - four for a brilliant victory, three for a victory, two for a tactical victory.
- Or take Lida (20,3), Grodno (2,4) and Baranowicze (22,19).

briliant.text:
The junctions held long enough and the 16th Army is on the Berezina with its guns, its wounded and its staff. Minsk was given up on order, in daylight, with the last train out before the demolition party fired the water tower.

The front now runs where it will run all winter. That is not a victory and I have not written it up as one; it is the difference between a defeated army and a destroyed one, and this autumn there is nothing behind us to replace a destroyed one with.

Their proclamation to the inhabitants of the former Grand Duchy is already posted in Minsk. It promises self-determination. The estates it does not mention are being handed back this week.

The Stolpce crossing went first and the whole line unhinged from it. The 16th Army is across the Berezina in the sense that its men are on the eastern bank; its artillery is not, and neither is a third of its transport.

Byelorussia is lost as far as the river and there is no formation west of it that answers to us any more.

intro:
Dyneburg: the Latgale winter

January 3rd, 1920

Minus twenty-five degrees, snow to the waist off the roads, and not a machine on either side that will start without a fire under it. The 15th Army holds Dyneburg with fortified positions, minefields and men who have been in them since November.

The attack is a Polish one with the Latvian army coming up from the north-west, and its purpose is political before it is military: to put Latgale into Riga's hands and cut the wire between us and Kaunas. Smigly-Rydz has the 1st and 3rd Legion divisions and the weather with him, because we are the ones who must sit still in it.

The town will be given up if it must be. What may not be given up is the corps, and what must be kept to the hour is the crossing and the two positions covering it, so that the guns and the field hospitals go out on the ice road instead of being left in the snow. Their own aerodrome and railhead lie behind the attack, and a raid on them would end the operation before it starts.

Victory conditions:
- Hold Laci (31,9), Cietoksnis (15,13), Gajoks Castle (24,20) and Dyneburg (20,26) at the last turn - four for a brilliant victory, three for a victory, two for a tactical victory.
- Or take Tilti Aerodrome (5,1), Rubeniski (20,1) and the Dyneburg-Wilno railway (19,35).

briliant.text:
The positions held to the last hour and the corps came out along the ice road with everything that could be pulled.

Dyneburg is Latvian now, which was the point of the whole affair; Warsaw handed the town to Riga within the month and got a treaty for it. Our men walked out of a fortified line in January without breaking, which is a harder thing than it reads.

The Latvians will make peace with us in the spring - they have what they wanted and no appetite for Pilsudski's larger idea. That leaves one enemy on this front instead of two, and it is the only good news in the report.

The 15th Army has lost the best part of two divisions to cold and capture, and the north-eastern flank of the front is open all the way to Polotsk.

intro:
Zhitomir: the Polish blow

April 25th, 1920

It has begun, and it has begun where the front was thinnest. Three Polish armies and Petliura's two divisions came through the 12th and 14th Armies this morning on a hundred-verst frontage, and the 12th Army is not so much retreating as coming apart into detachments.

The purpose is not Kiev. The purpose is a Ukrainian state under Petliura that will hold the Dnieper for Warsaw, and the price agreed for it in Warsaw last week was eastern Galicia and western Volhynia - which is to say Petliura sold four million Ukrainians to buy an army, and the villages here know it. That is the whole weakness of the enterprise, and in six weeks it will be the whole reason it fails.

For now they have the initiative, the railways and the better cavalry. I am to slow them on the Korosten-Zhitomir-Kazatin triangle so that the 12th and 14th can be got behind the Dnieper and the reserves coming from the Caucasus can be unloaded east of it. Six towns. Hold as many as I can to the last turn.

Victory conditions:
- Hold Korosten (23,2), Malin (34,8), Radomysl (34,13), Zhitomir (20,19), Fastov (42,26) and Kazatin (24,33) at the last turn - five for a brilliant victory, four for a victory, three for a tactical victory.
- Or take their forward positions at (3,6) and Polonne (2,21).

briliant.text:
Five of the six were still ours when the relief came up, and the 12th Army is behind the river instead of in their bag.

They will have Kiev inside a fortnight; that was settled by the frontage, not by this battle. What was settled here is that they will have it with our field armies intact in front of them and a rail net they have to repair before they can use it.

The First Cavalry Army is on the march from the Caucasus. Fourteen thousand sabres, and they are coming the whole way on their own horses.

The triangle went in three days. Korosten first, and after Korosten there was no lateral railway left and the two armies were fighting separate wars a hundred versts apart.

The 12th Army has lost its artillery park and most of a rifle division taken whole. There is no organised force between here and the Dnieper crossings.

intro:
The Dnieper crossings

May 5th, 1920

The order is to give up Kiev without fighting for it, and I have read it three times.

It is the right order. The city is a salient with one river at its back and their cavalry already north of it at Chernobyl; a garrison left in it would be a garrison lost, and the 12th Army is worth more to the Republic than the honour of the streets. So the army goes over to the eastern bank and the bridgeheads are held open behind it until the last battery is across.

My detachment is the rearguard. We have the demolition parties, the mined roads, the wire and the blockhouses, and almost nothing that moves - the cavalry went east three days ago. Their advance guard is racing us for the crossings and the Ukrainian division is coming up on the southern road to be first into the city for the politics of it.

Hold the crossings until the clock runs out. If their leading squadrons over-run themselves, the crossing they are riding for can be taken from them instead.

Victory conditions:
- Hold the crossings at (22,12) and (29,13) at the last turn - both for a brilliant victory, one for a victory or a tactical victory.
- Or take their crossing at (24,16).

briliant.text:
The army is over. Guns, trains, the wounded, the Kiev arsenal's machine tools on flatcars, and the last of the bridge guard on the last span before it went into the river.

They entered the city on the seventh and found the administration gone, the bridges down and no enemy to defeat. Petliura's people expected a rising in their favour; what they got was a population that has seen four armies in three years and has stopped coming out to meet any of them.

Their front is now four hundred versts from its railheads, holding a river line with cavalry it does not have. Ours is on the far bank with the Konarmia marching towards it.

They were on the crossing before the tail of the column. The pontoons went with the engineers still on them and what was left on the western bank had to break up and go north through the marshes in small parties.

The 12th Army has lost its bridging train, its heavy artillery and any claim to be a formation. There will be no counteroffensive from this front for a long time.

intro:
The Red tide

June 4th, 1920

The Konarmia is up. Fourteen thousand sabres that walked from the Kuban to the Dnieper in fifty-three days, and tomorrow morning they go into the seam between their 3rd and 6th Armies at Samhorodok.

The whole Polish position rests on a front too long for the troops holding it, supplied through a rail net we tore up in May, in a country where the requisition parties have already turned the villages against them. Break the crust anywhere and there is nothing behind it but staffs and depots. That is the theory. It is also, this once, the fact.

My task is the railway line behind the breach. Not their field army - it will not stand to be fought - but the junctions and stations it must have to withdraw in order: Zhitomir and Berdichev first, then Korosten, Fastov and Kazatin. Take them all and their two armies have to come out across country on their feet.

Victory conditions:
- Take Korosten (23,2), Malin (34,8), Zwiahel (4,10), Zhitomir (20,18), Fastov (41,25), Kazatin (24,33) and the junction at (40,7).

briliant.text:
Every junction on the list is ours and their 3rd Army came out of Kiev on the roads with our cavalry on both sides of it.

At Zhitomir the corps depot went up, five thousand of our people came out of the gaol, and the telegraph office was taken with the operators still at the keys - which is why their army group commander spent two days issuing orders to units that no longer had a line to hear them on.

Kiev is ours again on the twelfth. From here the Southwestern Front goes for Lvov and the Western Front for Warsaw, and there begins the argument that will cost us the campaign.

The breakthrough was made and then not exploited. They got their rearguards onto the junctions ahead of us, ran their trains out, and pulled back to the Sluch in order.

We hold the ground and they keep their army, which is the wrong way round. This front will not get another chance like the fifth of June.

intro:
Before Warsaw: the Wkra

August 13th, 1920

Read the orders in the order they were written and you can see the disaster coming.

The 4th Army and Gai's cavalry corps are to swing north-west around Warsaw. The 1st Cavalry Army is to go for Lvov, four hundred versts away, and has been told twice to come north and has not come. Between the two halves of our own front there is a gap of a hundred and fifty versts held by nothing, our men have marched six hundred versts from their railheads on what they could take from the villages, and the Polish workers who were supposed to rise have instead volunteered by the hundred thousand, because an army coming over the Vistula does not look like a revolution from underneath - it looks like Russia.

I am on the Wkra with the 15th Army's left. Sikorski's 5th Army is attacking into our flank from Modlin and there is a counterstroke forming south of the city that will be behind us by the sixteenth. My task is not the capital. My task is that this army group does not end up in the bag: hold the northern towns while the trains and the wounded go east, and get the divisional cores out through the crossings behind us.

Four of the designated formations out through the eastern exits and three of them still alive - only the designated formations may use an exit. Take Modlin and Legionowo instead if their line north of the city can be broken.

Victory conditions:
- Bring 4 of the designated formations off the map at (43,18), (43,24), (43,26) or (43,28), keeping at least 3 of them alive.
- Or hold Ciechanow (15,2), Szczytno (3,4), Plonsk (5,10), Siennica (21,10), Rozan (39,10), Pultusk (27,13), Nasielsk (16,18) and Radzymin (31,23) at the last turn - six for a brilliant victory, five for a victory, four for a tactical victory.
- Or take Szczypiorno (6,22), Stary Modlin (11,25) and Legionowo (19,27).

briliant.text:
The task set me is done. The cores are out east of the Bug with their staffs and their colours, the trains went before them, and the line north of the city held long enough that nothing of mine was cut off in it.

The operation as a whole has failed and I will not write it up otherwise. The counterblow from the Wieprz went in on the sixteenth into a hundred and fifty versts of nothing and rolled up the whole southern half of the front; four divisions of the 4th Army, out of touch with everyone including each other, crossed into East Prussia and were interned. That was decided in July, by the decision to run two offensives on divergent axes with one army's worth of supply, and it was not decided here.

What was decided here is how many of us came back. We are to cover the withdrawal to the Niemen.

The Wkra line went and with it the eastern road. What could not get out is in the encirclement between Nasielsk and the river, and I have no returns from it and expect none.

There is no army group on this front any more, only its remnants, and Warsaw is dictating terms to a front that cannot refuse them. My command is at an end.

intro:
Komarow: the Konarmia breaks out

August 31st, 1920

The Konarmia was ordered north on the eleventh, argued for four days, and turned north on the twentieth with Warsaw already lost. It has spent the last week riding into a pocket that closed behind it, and this morning the Polish 1st Cavalry Division is astride the eastern road at Komarow with the 13th Infantry coming up behind it.

So the last great cavalry battle of this war is being fought over a road junction, because everything else has already been decided. Twelve regiments of ours against six of theirs, in fog, on ploughed fields, at the sabre - and the arithmetic does not help us, because they are between us and the east and we have to go through them and they only have to stand.

Budyonny's order is to break out to the east and keep the army. Mine is the same, written smaller: hold the northern road while the transport and the wounded clear it, and take the designated divisions out through the eastern edge. Only those formations may use an exit. If Komarow itself can be taken the road opens for everybody.

Victory conditions:
- Bring 4 of the designated formations off the map at (27,12), (27,17) or (27,22), keeping at least 3 of them alive.
- Or hold Miaczyn (12,6), Niewirkow (24,6) and Wolica Brzozowa (5,10) at the last turn - three for a brilliant victory, two for a victory, one for a tactical victory.
- Or take Wolica Sniatycka (13,12) and Komarow (11,19).

briliant.text:
We are through. The divisions are east of Komarow, the transport went out ahead of them, and the army that was supposed to be destroyed here is on the Bug in the morning.

It cost us the horses. Whole squadrons came out leading them and a cavalry army without remounts is a rifle division that eats more; the Konarmia will not fight another action like this one, and by October it will be marching south against Wrangel instead, which is where it should have gone in June.

The Poles are calling Komarow their victory and by the ground they are right. But the First Cavalry Army came out of the pocket, and pockets are supposed to keep what goes into them.

The eastern road stayed shut. What did not get out at Komarow got out in squadrons and half-squadrons over the next four days, without guns, without transport, and without any of the four field hospitals.

The First Cavalry Army has been destroyed as an operational formation. There is nothing left on the southern face of this front to cover the withdrawal with.

intro:
The Niemen

September 20th, 1920

Six weeks ago this army was at the gates of Warsaw. It is now digging on the Niemen with eight thousand rifles where it had thirty, and the peace conference has already opened at Riga.

That last fact is the whole shape of this battle. Both governments know the line where the war stops will be roughly the line the armies stand on when it stops, so every verst held into October is a verst at the table, and Warsaw is attacking now precisely because the Entente is about to impose an armistice on them.

They are coming at Grodno frontally and sending a group north through Lithuanian territory - a neutral country whose border they have decided not to notice - to come out at Lida behind us. My task is the line itself: the crossings, the two railway towns and the junctions south of them, held to the last turn. If their northern group can be cut off against the Augustow canal, better still.

Victory conditions:
- Hold Orany (27,6), Werenow (40,8), Druskieniki (17,12), Lida (40,15), Wasiliszki (32,18), Grodno (15,20), Mosty (27,26) and Wolkowysk (26,35) at the last turn - six for a brilliant victory, five for a victory, four for a tactical victory.
- Or take Augustow (1,17), Brzostowica Wielka (19,33), Bialystok (4,35) and the crossing at (8,24).

briliant.text:
The line is where it was on the twentieth. They came through Lithuania as expected, arrived at Lida a day late and found a division waiting on the ground they meant to arrive behind.

Riga has the news within the day and it is worth more there than here. The delegation reports that the map on the table stopped moving this week.

The Lithuanians have protested the violation of their territory to the League and will be answered with a mutiny that nobody in Warsaw will admit ordering. Their turn comes in three weeks.

lose.text:
Grodno was turned from the north and the whole line came off the river with it. We are back on the Molodeczno road and the delegation at Riga has been told to expect worse terms than it was offered a week ago.

The army I brought out of Poland has been used up covering the ground I was told to hold.

intro:
Back to Minsk

October 9th, 1920

The preliminary peace was signed at Riga three days ago and the guns stop on the eighteenth. Nine days.

This morning General Zeligowski's division mutinied, on orders nobody in Warsaw will ever put in writing, and took Wilno from the Lithuanians as a private enterprise. That is the kind of week this is. On our sector both sides are doing the same arithmetic: whatever is held on the eighteenth is what the commission will draw a line around next spring.

So we go forward one last time, not for Minsk - the city is already behind our line - but for the road and rail junctions west of it that the frontier commission will otherwise hand across. Hold what we have and take what we can reach in nine days. Then it is over, and this front becomes a border.

Victory conditions:
- Hold Molodeczno (13,2), Radoszkowicze (26,10), Zaslaw (27,18) and Kojdanow (23,35) at the last turn - four for a brilliant victory, three for a victory, two for a tactical victory.
- Or take Wolozyn (2,14) and the junction at (0,27).

briliant.text:
The junctions are ours and the guns stopped with our people standing on them.

The treaty that follows in March gives Poland western Byelorussia and western Volhynia, and gives us the rest of Byelorussia, the Ukraine and six years without a war in the west. It is not a good peace. It is a peace the Republic could not have got in August, when it was being offered the Curzon line and turned it down because it thought it was about to take Warsaw.

Petliura's people are interned. Balakhovich's are still in the marshes and will be cleared out by December. The Konarmia went south a month ago and Wrangel is finished in the Crimea by November.

That is the end of it. Twenty months, from a screen in the Lithuanian forests to a frontier post outside Minsk, and the frontier post is the victory - not because we wanted this line, but because the Republic is still standing behind it. The campaign is over.

We could not get onto the junctions before the ceasefire hour and the commission will draw its line accordingly - west of Molodeczno instead of east of Wolozyn, with a hundred thousand people on the wrong side of it.

The war is over and the Republic has survived it, which is more than seemed likely in August. I would have liked to hand the delegation a better map. The campaign is over.
